title: Horseback-riding trip
titleCn: 骑马旅行周末攻略对话

paragraphs.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions one to six.
Hi, Greg. Great to see you. And thanks for emailing me with the details of the horseback riding trip you went on. I looked at the website, and it looks great.
Yeah. I went on the two-day mini break. Is that what you're thinking about?
Yes, that's the one.
Do you think they'd have places now in July, or will it be full?
If you can, hang on till September. That's when I went, and it was a really great time to go. It's not so hot for a start.
That'd suit me better anyway.
And also, at one point when we stopped for a picnic, I was lying in a field looking up and saw a huge flock of birds. They were obviously migrating. That's another reason why it's a good time to go.
Oh, great.
Oh, and another thing, you don't stay in a hotel. You stay in a tent, so you don't have to come back to town in the evening.
I'm up for that.
So where do you go on the first day?

Through some amazing wooded valleys full of chestnut and beech trees, but that's just the morning. Where you're really heading for is the mountains. And when you set out, you can only see them in the far distance. You don't actually get there until sunset.
Is it hard work riding all day?

No. The pace is easy, and there are plenty of breaks built in for picnics and even a snooze. But on that first evening, when you've been riding all day, you get the opportunity to go for a swim, and you really enjoy that. So relaxing.
And what's on day two? You said something about the national park.

No. Day two, you go up this incredible valley. At the end of it, there's a waterfall. It's an amazing place to stop for lunch. We even spotted an eagle while we were sitting there. And in the afternoon, there's a trip that goes to a cave. You can even ride into it.
Wow, that sounds great. I can't wait.
Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions seven to ten.
Now listen and answer questions seven to ten.
Okay. So what are your tips for a horseback riding weekend?

Well, I'd had a sore knee before I went, and I was pretty worried about that. It was okay actually, but what you've got to watch for is that you don't have any trouble with your back. Riding can really aggravate that.
No problem there. And comfortable clothes, I guess.

Yeah. But another thing I hadn't realized is that you actually walk the horses down some pretty steep and uneven paths. So make sure you have walking boots, not just normal riding boots. And even if you're going in the autumn, make sure you don't get sunburned. Even if it looks cloudy, take sunscreen, lots of it.
I think you've convinced me to sign up. When I was looking at the website, I saw that if I register online, I can get a discount. Did you do that or go through a travel agency?
I registered online, of course.

I just have to let my boss know when I want to take time off. And then the other important thing I read was that you have to make sure that your insurance company know that you're going on an adventure trip to make sure that you're covered in case anything happens.
I'm sure it won't, but better be safe than sorry.
That is the end of part one. You now have one minute to check your answers to part one.
